title: As France faces populist surge, voters' desire for radical change remains ambiguous
subhead: France appears increasingly permeated by feelings that make it ripe for a populist shift, but such a transformation is not inevitable, writes Brice Teinturier, deputy director general of polling firm Ipsos, drawing on findings from Le Monde's first poll.

title: 'The Abraham Accords have fueled war rather than peace in the Middle East'
subhead: The agreements were signed six years ago, but instead of leading to a broader normalization between Israel and the Arab world, they have instead deepened divisions in the Middle East, analyzes columnist Jean-Pierre Filiu.

title: Céline Dion returns to stage for first Paris show: 'I want to sing for you, to sing about life'
subhead: With a controlled voice and a relatively understated show, the Québécois star delighted the 30,000 spectators at the Plenitude Arena just outside the French capital with a 25-song set over two hours and 15 minutes. It was her first concert in six years.

title: Former Greek prison island of Gyaros becomes biodiversity haven
subhead: In the heart of the Cyclades archipelago, this island, long used as a place of exile, has been transformed into a sanctuary for wildlife, especially Mediterranean monk seals. The marine area is now officially protected under a presidential decree.

title: Hedge funds increasingly speculate on French debt, raising specter of crisis
subhead: Hedge funds now account for more than half of all European bond trading. France, which carries one of the highest debt levels in Western Europe, has become concerned about these creditors, whose profiles are less predictable than those of public institutions, banks or insurers.
